title.zh: 圆柱速度空间积分权重

summary: From strictly increasing normalized radial-speed and axial-velocity meshes, build the ghost-extended half-cell faces, the annular radial measure, the (nvr, nvx) cylindrical cell volumes, the ghosted finite-volume difference coefficients, the speed squared, and the positive/negative axial index ranges. This is the N1 preparation relation whose volume output is the cylindrical_volume port consumed by the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average.

identity.relation: the cylindrical velocity-space quadrature of a normalized (vr, vx) mesh: ghost-extended cell faces, annular radial measure, cell volumes, ghosted finite-volume coefficients, speed squared and axial sign index ranges
identity.direction: vr, vx -> radial_measure, radial_four_pi_measure, dvx, vr_left, vr_right, vx_left, vx_right, volume, inv_dvx_ghost, vx_over_dvx_ghost, vr_over_dvr_ghost, speed_squared, positive/negative vx index ranges
identity.definition: The radial mesh is extended by mirroring the last node (2*vr[-1] - vr[-2]) and the axial mesh by mirroring both ends; cell faces are midpoints of adjacent extended nodes with the innermost radial face fixed at zero. radial_measure = pi*(r_right^2 - r_left^2), volume = radial_measure[:, None] * dvx[None, :], radial_four_pi_measure = 4/3*pi*(r_right^3 - r_left^3). The ghosted arrays carry 1/dvx, vx/dvx and vr/dvr in their interior and exact zeros on the boundary shell. The index ranges locate strictly positive and strictly negative axial velocities.
identity.model: discrete finite-volume construction on the saved source's ghost-face convention; no distribution, collision model or field model is evaluated
identity.geometry: velocity space, cylindrical: radial speed vr (inner face at zero) and axial velocity vx; the azimuthal angle is integrated out into the pi*(r_right^2 - r_left^2) measure
identity.coordinates: vr and vx in whatever normalized velocity unit the caller works in; no unit conversion is performed
identity.boundary: the innermost radial face is exactly zero; the outermost faces are midpoints between the last node and its mirrored ghost; the ghosted coefficient arrays are exactly zero on their boundary shell; vx must contain both strictly negative and strictly positive entries
assumptions: The meshes are already expressed in the caller's normalized velocity unit, consistent with the normalization temperature convention of the downstream consumers.
The ghost faces follow the saved source's half-cell extrapolation convention; callers whose scheme expects different face placements must not reuse the measure unreviewed.
The azimuthal measure is exact for the annulus (pi times the squared-face difference), not a midpoint rule in vr.

Non-finite mesh points are rejected. The saved implementation checked only monotonicity and sizes, propagating NaN silently although its own document declared the fail-closed finite contract; this is the one documented repair.

inputs.name: vr
inputs.description: Normalized radial-speed mesh of the velocity grid.
inputs.constraints: A finite, strictly increasing, nonnegative one-dimensional array of length at least two. vr is a radial-speed axis: a negative node would make the annular measure negative, so the domain is restricted to nonnegative meshes.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.description: Normalized axial-velocity mesh of the velocity grid.
inputs.constraints: A finite, strictly increasing one-dimensional array of length at least two that contains at least one strictly negative and one strictly positive entry.

outputs.name: radial_measure
outputs.description: Annular radial measure pi*(r_right^2 - r_left^2) per radial cell.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for accepted input.

outputs.name: radial_four_pi_measure
outputs.description: Full-sphere measure 4/3*pi*(r_right^3 - r_left^3) per radial cell.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for accepted input.

outputs.name: dvx
outputs.description: Axial cell widths from the ghost-extended faces.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for accepted input.

outputs.name: vr_left
outputs.description: Inner radial face of each radial cell (first entry exactly zero).

outputs.name: vr_right
outputs.description: Outer radial face of each radial cell.

outputs.name: vx_left
outputs.description: Inner axial face of each axial cell (ghost-extended at the ends).

outputs.name: vx_right
outputs.description: Outer axial face of each axial cell (ghost-extended at the ends).

outputs.name: volume
outputs.description: Cylindrical cell volumes, rows matched to vr and columns to vx; the cylindrical_volume port of the downstream consumers.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for accepted input.

outputs.name: inv_dvx_ghost
outputs.description: 1/dvx in a ghost-extended (nvr+2, nvx+2) array, exact zeros on the boundary shell.

outputs.name: vx_over_dvx_ghost
outputs.description: vx/dvx in a ghost-extended (nvr+2, nvx+2) array, exact zeros on the boundary shell.

outputs.name: vr_over_dvr_ghost
outputs.description: vr/dvr in a ghost-extended (nvr+2, nvx+2) array, exact zeros on the boundary shell.

outputs.name: speed_squared
outputs.description: vr^2 + vx^2 on the mesh nodes.

outputs.name: positive_vx_indices
outputs.description: Indices of strictly positive axial velocities.

outputs.name: negative_vx_indices
outputs.description: Indices of strictly negative axial velocities.

preconditions: The caller works in a single normalized velocity unit for both meshes and downstream consumers.
The downstream scheme accepts the saved source's ghost-face and sign-index conventions.
supported: Constructing the cylindrical cell-volume measure that the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average normalizes against.
Ghosted finite-volume coefficients for schemes that consume 1/dvx, vx/dvx and vr/dvr with a zero boundary shell.
Sign index ranges for flux-split axial updates.
Nonuniform meshes: the annular measure stays exact for the ghost-face construction.
excluded: Mesh generation or adaptation: the meshes are caller inputs.
Any distribution, collision or field model.
Schemes whose cell faces differ from the saved source's ghost-face convention.
Unit conversion between normalized velocity and m/s; that scale is the caller's.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError with a message naming the quantity when vr or vx is not a real numeric finite strictly increasing one-dimensional array of length at least two, when vr has a negative entry (vr is a radial-speed axis; a negative node would make the annular measure negative), or when vx does not contain both strictly negative and strictly positive velocities. Boolean, string and complex arrays are not coerced.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the quadrature outputs are not representable in double precision for finite inputs that satisfy the stated domain -- for example a radial mesh at 1e308 whose mirrored ghost face and squared faces overflow to infinity, or an axial ghost face beyond the float64 ceiling -- and when the annular measures, the four-pi measure, the axial widths or the volumes underflow to exact zero (for example a radial mesh at 0 and 1e-200 whose squared faces underflow), contradicting the strictly-positive output contract. There is no callback and no iteration.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no fields.

example.description: Build the quadrature of a small normalized mesh, check the hand-derived annular measure and ghost shells, and feed the volume into the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature
from scirel.collisions import average_cross_section_over_maxwellian

vr = np.array([0.5, 1.5])
vx = np.array([-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5])
result = make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature(vr=vr, vx=vx)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['radial_measure'], [np.pi, 3.0 * np.pi], rtol=0, atol=0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result['vx_left'], [-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0], rtol=0, atol=0)
assert np.all(result['inv_dvx_ghost'][0, :] == 0.0)
assert np.all(result['inv_dvx_ghost'][1:-1, 1:-1] == 1.0)
assert result['positive_vx_first_index'] == 2
rate = average_cross_section_over_maxwellian(
    particle_energy_ev=np.array([0.0, 10.0]),
    particle_mass_amu=1.0,
    target_temperature_ev=10.0,
    target_mass_amu=2.0,
    vx=vx,
    vr=vr,
    tnorm_ev=20.0,
    cylindrical_volume=result['volume'],
    cross_section_m2=lambda energy: np.full_like(energy, 3.0e-20),
)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(rate)) and np.all(rate > 0.0)
try:
    make_cylindrical_velocity_quadrature(vr=vr, vx=np.array([1.0, np.nan, 2.0]))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'vx' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a non-finite mesh must be rejected')
example.expected: radial_measure is exactly [pi, 3*pi] for the ghost faces [0, 1], [1, 2]; the axial ghost faces extend by half a cell on both ends; the ghosted coefficient arrays are zero on their boundary shell and 1/dvx in the interior; the strictly positive axial indices start at 2; the volume feeds the Maxwellian rate average to finite positive rates; and a NaN mesh point raises ValueError naming vx.

scope: That the public callable reproduces the saved source's field set, shapes and index semantics exactly ( eighteen output fields asserted by name ).
The hand-derived oracle on a different mesh than the saved package test: annular measures, ghost-extended faces, dvx, volume, speed squared and sign indices, exact to floating point.
The box-partition closure: the total volume equals the annulus up to the ghost face times the ghosted axial span.
Nonuniform radial meshes: the annular measure stays exact for the ghost-face construction, including the mirrored outer face.
The ghosted coefficient arrays are exactly zero on the boundary shell and carry 1/dvx, vx/dvx and vr/dvr in the interior.
The composition contract: the volume feeds the Maxwellian relative-speed rate average to finite positive rates.

The input contract: finite strictly increasing nonnegative meshes of length at least two, both axial signs required; NaN and infinite meshes are rejected by parameter name, and a negative radial node (which would make the annular measure negative) is rejected. Non-finite input rejection is a documented repair; the saved implementation propagated NaN silently.

Output representability: meshes near the float64 ceiling (radial 1e308 with a mirrored ghost face, or an axial ghost beyond the ceiling) are rejected with a ValueError instead of returning non-finite measures or volumes, and meshes whose squared faces underflow to zero (radial 0 and 1e-200) are rejected instead of returning zero measures. Ordinary positive meshes produce unchanged numbers.

Bounded historical replay against the saved KN1DPy implementation, pinned by SHA-256, reproducing every field on two meshes at rtol 1e-15 plus the repair differential witness. This replay is environment-gated and is historical development evidence, not qualified-L1 provenance.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained tests establish the construction against hand-derived values, the partition closure, the ghost-shell contract, the composition with the Maxwellian rate average, and the input contract including the documented repairs. The separately executed intake replay establishes bounded numerical agreement with the saved KN1DPy implementation on the compared meshes only. No test establishes that the ghost-face convention is the right discretization for any downstream scheme beyond the consumers documented here, that any caller mesh is physically valid, or that the source project behaves correctly outside the compared domain. KN1DPy's strict D1 qualification is withdrawn; the saved bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only. Expert recognition, version-level trust and distribution licensing remain pending.
known_limitations: The outer faces use the saved source's half-cell extrapolation (mirror the last node); schemes expecting different face placements must not reuse the measure unreviewed.
The asset performs no unit conversion: the meshes and every output share the caller's normalized velocity unit, and the physical thermal-speed scale is the caller's.

Non-finite and non-real mesh rejection are documented development repairs, not source behavior: a caller migrating from the saved implementation sees a ValueError where it previously saw coercion, an unrelated TypeError or a silently corrupted quadrature. The same holds for the nonnegative radial domain and the output representability check: a negative or float64-ceiling mesh that the saved implementation accepted with negative or non-finite measures is rejected here.
The nonnegative radial domain makes the saved source's positive-radial-speed convention explicit; a caller that believes a signed radial axis is meaningful is looking at a different relation.

The saved bundle sits in the re-review archive and KN1DPy's strict D1 qualification is withdrawn; the historical replay evidence cannot be upgraded to qualified-L1 provenance without a new strict freeze and independent review of the source project.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
